title: Gaussian isoperimetric inequality
statement: Let $n$ be a nonnegative integer, let $A\subseteq\mathbb R^n$ be measurable, and let $\alpha\in(0,1)$ equal the standard Gaussian measure of $A$. Then the Gaussian profile $U(\alpha)$, converted to an extended nonnegative real, is at most the Gaussian surface area of $A$, defined by the lower limit of its scaled rotation sensitivities as the rotation angle tends to zero from above.
hypotheses_covered: The standard Gaussian measure of $A$ has real value $\alpha$
replaced: Let $n\ge0$, let $\gamma_n$ be standard Gaussian measure on $\mathbb R^n$, and let $G,G\prime$ be independent vectors with law $\gamma_n$. Write $s_A(t)$ for the real value of the product-measure mass $(\gamma_n\otimes\gamma_n)\{(g,h):\mathbf1_A(g)\ne\mathbf1_A(\cos t\,g+\sin t\,h)\}$. Write $P_\gamma(A)=\liminf_{t\to0^+}\bigl[\sqrt{\pi/2}\,s_A(t)/t\bigr]_+$ in $[0,\infty]$, where $[x]_+=\max(x,0)$. For every measurable $A\subseteq\mathbb R^n$ of Gaussian volume $\alpha\in(0,1)$, $\varphi(\Phi^{-1}(\alpha))\le P_\gamma(A)$, where $\varphi$ and $\Phi$ are the standard Gaussian density and distribution function.
